note: THE PUBLIC EVENT PAGE: NO PAYMENT LINK, NO WAY TO CLAIM, AND A BUTTON THAT LIED. The founder created 'crusade bangladesh' on his own tenant, priced a $50 adult ticket, chose REVOLUT because that URL is configured, registered, and reported: "i pressed on pay but it did not brought me to the payment page but to the payment confirmation directly. there is no confirm button in inbox, only in event page." Four defects, and three of them are one hole seen from three sides. ONE - THE BUTTON PROMISED A PROCESSOR THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. requiresPayment in the submit route is amount > 0 && !waitlisted && !manualConfirmationMode(), and manualConfirmationMode() is statically true while PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED is a false module constant, so no Checkout session is created, no url comes back and the redirect 'Continue to payment' and 'Redirecting to payment...' both PROMISED cannot happen. The copy is now DERIVED FROM THE SAME CONSTANT THAT DECIDES THE BEHAVIOUR rather than describing it from memory, so the two cannot drift and the day a rail lands the promise returns with the thing it promises. It still names the price, because the registrant is about to owe money; what is removed is the claim about where they are about to be sent. TWO - THE STRIPE RETURN BRANCH STAYS, GATED, AND THE GATE IS THE POINT. Reported rather than guessed: it is NOT deleted, because PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED is a real switch with a real day to be flipped and deleting the branch means whoever flips it ships a checkout that returns to a registration form; and it is NOT left as it was, because '?registration=success' IS A URL ANY VISITOR CAN TYPE and it rendered 'Payment received - you're registered!' to somebody who had paid nobody. That is a lie about money that needs no Stripe session, only a query string. So the effect that reads the param returns early unless PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED: the branch is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE rather than merely unused, and the condition that decides whether anyone is ever SENT to Checkout is the same one that decides whether the RETURN screen exists. THE-351's positional guard - the forbidden phrases may appear in that branch and nowhere else in the file - is untouched and still passes, and THE-355 adds the rendering half: the page is mounted at '?registration=success' and swept. THREE - THE CHURCH'S LINKS REACHED THE MEMBER APP AND NOT THE PUBLIC PAGE. THE-351 resolved givingLinks for /api/my-registrations, i.e. for the LOGGED-IN member, and this page rendered the reference code and the disclaimer and nothing else. The one screen that needed the link was the one screen without it. They are now resolved SERVER-SIDE in the route component, which already holds the tenant and the event, so there is no second round trip, no loading state and no failure mode; readGivingLinks re-validates every stored URL against the phishing allow-list on each request and resolveEventPaymentLinks can only ever NARROW what the church currently publishes, so a provider ticked for this event and since deleted cannot render as a dead tile. FOUR - A PUBLIC REGISTRANT COULD NOT CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY THE INBOX WAS EMPTY. THE-351 built the claim flow behind requireAuth and mounted it on UserEvents; its own ownership record names the hole it left - the admin's attendee row 'is the only surface that reaches a member who registered LOGGED OUT and can therefore never press I've paid themselves'. For a crusade, where most attendees have no account and never will, that is not an edge case, it is everybody. No claim was ever created, so the queue was empty, so the inbox correctly painted 'Nothing to confirm' about a thing that had never happened - and the founder read an empty state as an absent control. The inbox's Confirm button was never missing; it is asserted here as a no-regression, ALONGSIDE the assertion that an empty inbox is a DIFFERENT SCREEN, because a guard that rendered an empty inbox and looked for a button would have reported the founder's own bug as 'Confirm is missing' and sent someone to rebuild a button that was already there. HOW A LOGGED-OUT REGISTRANT CLAIMS, AND WHY NOT THE REFERENCE CODE (STOP condition 3). The reference is DISQUALIFIED TWICE OVER by facts this repository had already written down: event-payment-claims.ts records that it is deliberately 'a SECOND identifier that GRANTS NOTHING' precisely because IT IS WRITTEN INTO A PAYMENT NOTE, ON VENMO, WHOSE TRANSACTION FEED IS PUBLIC BY DEFAULT - so a reference that authorised a write would be a credential the feature PUBLISHES - and at 31^6 it is ~29.7 bits, a guessing target rather than a secret. Either fact alone settles it. So it is THE-324's shape, which solved this exact problem for rota invitations: a stored 256-bit token, no sign-in, authorising ONLY the fields it needs, 43 characters of base64url spelled by the same regex shape rota-invitations.ts pins. THE TOKEN SELECTS THE REGISTRATION RATHER THAN ACCOMPANYING AN ID: the public route accepts NO registrationId at all and looks the document up BY the token field, so there is no pair to mismatch and no check to forget - the strongest available statement about 'you cannot claim on another person's registration' is that there is no expressible request that names one. limit(2) rather than limit(1), THE-324's reading: two rows sharing a token would mean a collision or a hand-written value, and answering with an arbitrary one would let a token address a row it was not minted for, so the ambiguous case is REFUSED. The token is minted only for a seat that owes money, handed back ONCE to the person who just registered, held in component state rather than the URL or storage (it authorises a write against a document carrying a money amount; a URL lands in history, a referer and a screenshot, and a storage key outlives the tab), and read back out by no route on any surface. NO firestore.rules CHANGE (STOP condition 2 does not fire) AND NO INDEX (nor does 4's index half). The public claim is the Admin SDK inside a route, exactly as THE-351's authenticated one is and for the reason that route already records: the registration UPDATE rule requires manageEvents, and the alternative is loosening a rule on a document carrying a money amount in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS ON MERGE WITH NO EMULATOR TESTS - THE-313's one line turned 46 files red. One equality where() with no orderBy is a single-field index Firestore maintains automatically, so firestore.indexes.json - which does not deploy, and where an index would be INERT while the query threw failed-precondition in production - is untouched and asserted byte-identical alongside functions/ and src/app/layout.tsx. THE-355 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST ANYWHERE and asks rulesDigestFailure() like every other pinner, because THE-333 and THE-341 each spelled a copy and both turned THE-325 red. ../claim IS NOT LOOSENED TO COVER THE PUBLIC CASE. A signed-in member's claim is authenticated and should stay authenticated; widening that handler to also accept a bearer token would give one route two authorisation models and one branch to get wrong. Two doors, two locks, and neither can be mistaken for the other. The public route writes THE SAME THREE FIELDS and there is no branch in it that writes paymentStatus, paymentInvoiceId or amount - so the worst an unauthorised holder of a token can do is move ONE registration from unpaid to claimed and put its owner in front of an admin who then looks in their own bank account, which is the same blast radius THE-324 accepted for a rota invitation. 'confirmed' MEANT TWO THINGS ON ONE ROW. The founder's screenshot showed each attendee as 'confirmed' (a badge) AND 'Payment not confirmed' (a warning) with a Confirm button beside both. Both facts were TRUE - the badge is REGISTRATION status, the field that gates Check In and has never meant money, and the warning is PAYMENT state - but spelled with one word an admin cannot tell which one Confirm is about to change. THE REGISTRATION SIDE GIVES UP THE WORD AND THE PAYMENT SIDE KEEPS IT, because 'Confirm' is the founder's own word for the button, the correct verb for what the CHURCH does, and deliberately NOT in FORBIDDEN_CLAIM_PHRASES. The badge now reads 'Registered' and the stat above the list, which counts status === 'confirmed' and therefore SEATS rather than payments, reads 'Registered' too - '2 Confirmed' over two unpaid seats was the same collision one level up. THE STORED VALUES DO NOT MOVE: this is a display map, status still stores 'confirmed', every query still filters on it and check-in still gates on it, because renaming a stored enum to fix a label would be a migration on a live collection to solve a wording problem. AdminEvents.tsx IS DIGEST-PINNED AND THE PIN IS NOT SUBSTITUTED: THE_308_EVENTS.strippedSha and strippedLines are unchanged and the edit - three exact strings - is REVERSED before hashing by an APPENDED unwrap that runs first, so THE-313's, THE-317's, THE-324's and THE-326's reversals all still match what they were written against. main went red for everyone once because a PR replaced a pinned digest. CHECK-IN STILL NEVER BLOCKS ON PAYMENT and the shape is still what makes it true: the Check In control is gated on r.status === 'confirmed' and no payment field is read inside it, asserted by driving all four payment states through the real screen and finding an enabled control on every one. CONFIRM IS STILL IDEMPOTENT AND STILL CALLS THE-350's WRITER, asserted by pressing twice and counting invoices rather than by description, because this ticket adds a SECOND way for a claim to arrive and therefore a second way for two claims to land on one seat; a double invoice is a FALSE FINANCIAL RECORD that the church's books, the dashboard and the member's own giving statement would all repeat. FREE REGISTRATION IS ENTIRELY UNAFFECTED: amount > 0 still means a free seat, a waitlist entry and a ticket discounted to $0 never mint a reference, never mint a token and render no payment machinery at all, asserted through the real screen. A PAID EVENT WITH NO CONFIGURED LINK (STOP condition 6) SAYS THE TRUE THING RATHER THAN LEAVING A GAP - an event with a price and no way to pay is the original defect in a different costume. THE-351 made that state hard to reach from the admin side but it stays reachable two ways no form validation can close: a church that priced an event first and DELETED its links afterwards, and a stored link that no longer passes readGivingLinks on re-validation. So the member is told their place is booked, that the church has not published a payment link yet, to contact them quoting the reference, and that they will not be turned away at the door - and no claim control is offered, because there is nothing they could have paid. THE PRIMITIVES ARE SPENT AND THE ONE THE-351 REJECTED IS ADOPTED ON A CORRECTED PREMISE. THE-351's note said alert was rejected here because 'this shell is the public event page and carries none of the admin app's primitives'. The shadcn token layer is declared on bare :root in globals.css - --card, --foreground, --border and the rest - not inside an admin scope, so every primitive resolves on this page exactly as it does on an admin one. The copy was set in the page's own type for a reason that does not hold, and the accessible role was the cost. alert (role=alert) for the instruction, the no-links state and the claimed state; item for each payment link; separator for the rule. button is REJECTED for 'I've paid' because its default size is h-8 (32px) and its largest, lg, is h-9 (36px) - both UNDER the 44px tap floor below sm, the same finding THE-351 recorded for the inbox's own Confirm - so a plain button wearing min-h-11 and CONTROL_DENSITY.action mints no height of its own. card REJECTED: this is a notice inside a panel that is already a card. badge REJECTED: the instruction is three sentences and a badge is a label. empty REJECTED: it announces an absent COLLECTION, and a church that has published no link is a capability withheld over a registration that completely succeeded. dialog REJECTED: nothing here interrupts, and the registrant has already finished the only flow on the page. sonner REJECTED: a toast leaves the screen while a payment instruction must not. tooltip REJECTED: a phone has no hover, and a member who believes 'I've paid' settles the matter will arrive at the door believing they are paid, so the help text sits beside the button. NO npm dependency, NO theme token, NO new primitive (43 on disk, enumerated rather than assumed, accordion still the absent one) and NO colour literal: the claim button spends the tenant's own primaryColor, which this page already carries for every other action. EVERY CONTROL IS MEASURED IN A REAL CHROMIUM AT 380/768/1024/1280/1440 WITH TRANSITIONS AND ANIMATIONS SUPPRESSED, because #490 measured min-h-[44px] at 7.7469px mid-transition and a menu row at 41.79998779296875px - exactly 44 x 0.95, the first frame of zoom-in-95 - and getBoundingClientRect() reports the SCALED box. happy-dom has no layout engine, so a source-only assertion would pass on a broken screen. The payment LINK is measured as a tap target too: it is the control a person on a phone actually presses to leave for Revolut, and an anchor is as much a tap target as a button. EVERY CONTENT GREP RUNS OVER PARSER-STRIPPED SOURCE through #496's IMPORTED stripper, and every needle whose subject this ticket's own suites must also name is ASSEMBLED FROM FRAGMENTS, because #496 found TWO of its own guards SELF-MATCHING. No test pins a line number (THE-331 pinned a line that a deletion shifted, so the suite would have measured whatever landed there), no fixture is within 90 days of today (#468 turned main red for everyone), and nothing shells out to git (#454: a depth-1 clone has no base revision).

entries.why: THE-355 ADDS this route: a registrant with NO ACCOUNT says they paid. It exists as a SECOND door rather than as a loosening of ../claim, and that is the whole design decision: a signed-in member's claim is authenticated by verified uid or verified token email and must keep being, so widening that handler to also accept a bearer token would give one route two authorisation models and one branch to get wrong. STOP CONDITION 3 IS ANSWERED BY SHAPE, NOT BY A CHECK: this handler accepts NO registrationId, does not read one, and has nothing to compare one against - the document is FOUND BY THE TOKEN via .where(PUBLIC_CLAIM_TOKEN_FIELD, '==', token).limit(2), so the credential SELECTS the row rather than accompanying an id a forgotten check could let diverge from it. The strongest available statement about 'you cannot claim on another person's registration' is that there is no expressible request that names one. limit(2) rather than limit(1) is THE-324's reading and its reason: two documents sharing a token would mean a collision (at 256 bits it has not happened) or a hand-written value, and answering with an arbitrary one would let a token address a row it was not minted for, so the ambiguous case is refused. The shape is checked before Firestore is, so '?token=<a megabyte of junk>' never becomes a query. IT WRITES THE SAME THREE FIELDS AS ../claim AND NO MONEY STATE: there is no branch here that writes paymentStatus, paymentInvoiceId or amount, and paymentStateOf keys 'confirmed' on the INVOICE ID, which only the confirm route can write and only through THE-350's writer - so the worst an unauthorised holder of a token can do is move ONE registration from unpaid to claimed and put its owner in front of an admin who then opens their own bank account, the same blast radius THE-324 accepted for a rota invitation. NO firestore.rules CHANGE: it is the Admin SDK inside a route, exactly as ../claim is, because the registration UPDATE rule requires manageEvents and the alternative is loosening a rule on a document carrying a money amount in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS with no emulator tests. NO COMPOSITE INDEX: one equality where() with no orderBy is a single-field index Firestore maintains automatically, so firestore.indexes.json - not deployed, and where an index would be INERT while the query threw failed-precondition - is untouched. A MALFORMED TOKEN AND A MISSING TENANT GET ONE MESSAGE, because a response that distinguished them would confirm which half was right to whoever was guessing. The Firestore write is awaited BEFORE anything is notified and the notification's result never gates the response: a notification is a PROMPT, NEVER THE RECORD, so a church with an empty roster or a provider outage still has the person sitting in the inbox with everything needed to match a bank line. A failure answers 500 and writes nothing - THE-342's rule, a default that hides an error is a bug.

THE-355 EDITS this file, APPENDING and substituting nothing THE-351 wrote. Three additions, each the same rule one layer further out. (1) THE PUBLIC REGISTRANT'S COPY, separate from the member's rather than reused verbatim because the two audiences differ in one fact that changes the instruction: a signed-in member can reopen this ticket in My Events tomorrow and a logged-out registrant cannot, so this copy has to tell them to press now and say what the email they were just sent is for. Every string is swept by THE-351's existing Object.entries sweep the moment it is exported, which is why it lives here and not in the component. publicPayBody carries the founder's door decision in its own last sentence - 'Bring this ticket either way - you will not be turned away at the door' - because this screen is the only thing a logged-out registrant is guaranteed to read, and a first draft that dropped it was caught by the rendering test rather than by review. (2) THE CLAIM TOKEN'S SHAPE, and only its shape: PUBLIC_CLAIM_TOKEN_RE, the field name and the byte count. THE MINTER IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE - this module is imported by client components and must not pull in node:crypto, the same discipline buildPaymentReference already follows by taking its bytes as an argument, and the same split rota-invitations.ts makes between TOKEN_RE and lib/rota-invite.ts's newRotaToken. The header records why the REFERENCE CODE cannot do this job, in the file that already documents both halves of the reason: it is written into a payment note on Venmo, whose transaction feed is PUBLIC BY DEFAULT, so a reference that authorised a write would be a credential the feature publishes; and at 31^6 it is ~29.7 bits. (3) REGISTRATION_STATUS_LABEL and REGISTERED_STAT_LABEL, which is the disambiguation this module owes its own vocabulary: the payment feature took the word 'confirmed' for what the CHURCH does, and the registration status field had been rendering the same word raw since long before it. The payment side keeps the word because 'confirm' is the founder's own word for the button and is deliberately NOT in FORBIDDEN_CLAIM_PHRASES; the registration side gives it up for 'Registered', which is plainer and is what the number actually counts. IT IS A DISPLAY MAP AND NOT A MIGRATION: status still stores 'confirmed', every query still filters on it, check-in still gates on it, and an unrecognised status renders as ITSELF rather than blank so an admin can always see a state the map has not met.

THE-355 EDITS this file: it is the screen the founder was looking at. THE BUTTON'S COPY IS NOW DERIVED FROM THE GATE rather than describing it from memory - manualConfirmationMode() is what makes the redirect not happen, so it is what chooses the words, and the two cannot drift; it still names the price because the registrant is about to owe money, and what is removed is the claim about where they are about to be sent. THE STRIPE RETURN BRANCH STAYS, GATED ON PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED, and neither of the other two answers is honest: deleting it means whoever flips that switch ships a checkout that returns to a registration form, and leaving it is the defect, because '?registration=success' is a URL ANY VISITOR CAN TYPE and it rendered a payment confirmation to somebody who had paid nobody. Gated, no string inside either branch can render for any input, and the constant that decides whether anyone is ever SENT to Checkout is the same one that decides whether the RETURN screen exists. THE CHURCH'S LINKS AND THE CLAIM CONTROL land inside THE-351's own data-public-payment-note block, which its positional forbidden-phrase guard still finds. THE CLAIM TOKEN LIVES IN COMPONENT STATE AND NOWHERE ELSE - not localStorage, not the URL, not a cookie: it authorises a write against a document carrying a money amount, and a URL lands in browser history, a referer header and a shared screenshot while a storage key outlives the tab and the person; component state dies with the tab, which is exactly the lifetime of the screen that uses it. A FAILED CLAIM SURFACES VISIBLY AND LOSES NOTHING: THE-321's saveState shape, with `done` never cleared by the claim machine, so a rejected press leaves the ticket code, the reference and the links exactly where they were and adds a failure beside the button that can be retried. PRIMITIVES: alert for the instruction, the no-links state and the claimed state, adopted on a CORRECTED PREMISE - THE-351 rejected it here saying this shell 'carries none of the admin app's primitives', and the shadcn token layer is declared on bare :root in globals.css rather than in an admin scope, so every primitive resolves here exactly as it does on an admin screen and the accessible role was the cost of the mistake; item for each payment link, separator for the rule. button REJECTED for 'I've paid': default h-8 (32px), largest lg h-9 (36px), both under the 44px floor below sm. card, badge, empty, dialog, sonner and tooltip each REJECTED for a reason spelled at the call site. A link with no valid URL renders its handle or email rather than a dead anchor - the Zelle case, which has no per-church URL at all.

THE-355 EDITS this route component: it resolves the church's own payment links for THIS event and passes them to the page. THE FOUNDER CONFIGURED REVOLUT AND WAS NEVER SHOWN IT, because THE-351 resolved givingLinks for /api/my-registrations - the LOGGED-IN member app - and this file, which renders the page a public registrant actually lands on, passed branding and the event and nothing else. RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE RATHER THAN FETCHED BY THE CLIENT: this component already holds the tenant and the event, so a second round trip would add an API surface, a loading state and a failure mode to a page that has the answer in hand, which is the same reading my-registrations made. INTERSECTED ON EVERY READ AND NEVER TRUSTED FROM THE EVENT DOCUMENT: readGivingLinks re-runs the phishing allow-list over each stored URL, so a link that no longer passes simply stops being a link, and resolveEventPaymentLinks can only ever NARROW what the church currently publishes - a provider ticked for this event and since deleted from Donations cannot render as a dead tile, and an empty selection means all of them, which is the safe direction because an event created before that field existed must not render a paid ticket with nowhere to pay. The links are PUBLIC BY CONSTRUCTION - the same ones the church publishes on its own giving page - so nothing private crosses this boundary. THE PUBLIC URL SHAPE IS UNTOUCHED: the route segment, the tenant subdomain, the draft/cancelled gate and the deliberate withholding of discountCodes from the client all stand exactly as they were, and each is asserted, because https://{tenantId}.theharvest.app/event/{eventId} is public and may be printed on something.

THE-355 EDITS this route in one place: it mints the 256-bit claim token beside the reference code and hands it back once. THE MINT SITS INSIDE THE EXISTING owesManualPayment TERNARY AND NOWHERE ELSE, which is what makes 'a free registration acquires no credential' structural rather than a rule someone remembers - the same discipline the reference code already follows one line up, and the same reason: a free seat has nothing to claim and must not acquire the vocabulary of one. THE THREE EXISTING BYPASSES ARE UNTOUCHED: amount > 0 still means a free registration, a waitlist entry and a ticket discounted to $0 never reach this question, so a church running a free conference sees nothing this ticket added. IT IS randomBytes(PUBLIC_CLAIM_TOKEN_BYTES).toString('base64url') HERE RATHER THAN IN THE COPY MODULE, because that module is imported by client components and must not drag node:crypto into them; the module owns the SHAPE, which is what both ends have to agree on, exactly as rota-invitations.ts owns TOKEN_RE while lib/rota-invite.ts owns newRotaToken. THE TOKEN TRAVELS BACK EXACTLY ONCE, to the person who just pressed Register, and no other route on any surface reads it back out - my-registrations, the inbox route, the confirm route and the public claim route are each asserted not to return it, because a credential that a second read hands out is not a credential. Nothing else in this file moves: the Stripe branch, the capacity check, the discount accounting, the waitlist, the CRM activity and the confirmation email are all untouched.

THE-355 EDITS this file in THREE EXACT STRINGS - an import, the attendee badge's expression and the stat's label - and the smallness is deliberate, because this screen is pinned by a whole-file stripped digest and the edit has to be REVERSIBLE. APPENDED, NEVER SUBSTITUTED: THE_308_EVENTS.strippedSha and strippedLines in AdminMinistry.desktop-layout.test.tsx are UNCHANGED, and a new unwrap list reverses these three strings before hashing, running FIRST so THE-313's, THE-317's, THE-324's and THE-326's own reversals still match the file as each was written against. main went red for everyone once because a PR replaced a pinned digest, and THE-251's note names re-recording as the weaker option in its own words: 'it would bless every other byte that moved in the same breath, which is the one thing this guard exists to catch'. WHAT THE EDIT FIXES: the founder's screenshot showed each attendee as 'confirmed' (a badge) AND 'Payment not confirmed' (a warning) with a Confirm button beside both - one word for two different facts, so an admin could not tell what the button would change. Both facts were true: the badge renders registrations/{id}.status, which is REGISTRATION status and is what gates Check In, and the warning is payment state living in separate payment* fields no door control reads. The registration side gives up the word and now reads 'Registered'; the stat above the list, which counts status === 'confirmed' and therefore SEATS, is re-labelled in the same breath because '2 Confirmed' over two unpaid seats is the same collision one level up. NOTHING ABOUT THE MONEY OR THE DOOR MOVED: it is a display map, status still stores 'confirmed', firestorePathsOf is unchanged because this ticket adds no read and no write, and the Check In control is still gated on r.status === 'confirmed' with no payment field read inside it - asserted by driving all four payment states through the real screen and finding an enabled control on every one, because the founder's decision is that an unconfirmed guest walks in.

THE-355 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-351 owned the one before it, THE-350 the one before that and THE-349 the one before that. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 68 -> 69 and this ticket's guard suite joins RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-351's entry, NEVER OVER IT - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired, and the exact floor still may not shrink: a suite that quietly stopped pinning would still fail here. THE-355 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST ANYWHERE, and that is a finding rather than luck. A PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE AGAINST A DOCUMENT CARRYING A MONEY AMOUNT is the shape that most obviously needs a rule - and it needed none, for the same reason THE-351 found one layer in: the public claim is the Admin SDK inside a route, exactly as THE-351's authenticated one is, so the registration UPDATE rule requiring manageEvents is untouched and nothing is loosened in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS ON MERGE WITH NO EMULATOR TESTS, where THE-313's one-line change turned 46 files red. What stands in place of a rule is a STRONGER shape rather than a weaker one: the route accepts no registrationId at all and finds the document BY a stored 256-bit token - THE-324's rota-invitation pattern, no sign-in, authorising only the fields it needs - so there is no pair to mismatch, no ownership comparison to forget, and no expressible request that names somebody else's seat. THE-333 and THE-341 each spelled a copy of the rules digest and both turned THE-325 red; this ticket asks rulesDigestFailure() like every other pinner and spells nothing.
